verses.1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our refuge through all generations.
verses.2: Before the mountains were born, the earth and the world brought forth, from eternity to eternity you are God.
verses.3: But humans you return to dust, saying, "Return, you mortals!" 4c Before a watch passes in the night,
verses.4: A thousand years in your eyes are merely a yesterday,
verses.5: you have brought them to their end; They disappear like sleep at dawn; they are like grass that dies.
verses.6: It sprouts green in the morning; by evening it is dry and withered.
verses.7: Truly we are consumed by your anger, filled with terror by your wrath.
verses.8: You have kept our faults before you, our hidden sins exposed to your sight.
verses.9: Our life ebbs away under your wrath; our years end like a sigh.
verses.10: Seventy is the sum of our years, or eighty, if we are strong; Most of them are sorrow and toil; they pass quickly, we are all but gone.
verses.11: Who comprehends your terrible anger? Your wrath matches the fear it inspires.
verses.12: Teach us to count our days aright, that we may gain wisdom of heart.
verses.13: Relent, O LORD! How long? Have pity on your servants!
verses.14: Fill us at daybreak with your love, that all our days we may sing for joy.
verses.15: Make us glad as many days as you humbled us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
verses.16: Show your deeds to your servants, your glory to their children.
verses.17: May the favor of the Lord our God be ours. Prosper the work of our hands! Prosper the work of our hands!

notes.text: The translation reverses the order of the difficult Hebrew verses Psalm 90:3 and 4 to get the probable original order. A watch in the night: the night was divided into three sentry periods or watches. Cf Judges 7:19.
Return: one word of God is enough to return mortals to the dust from which they were created. Humans were created from earth in Genesis 2:7; 3:19.
You have brought them to their end: an interpretation of the unclear Hebrew.
It is dry and withered: the transitory nature of the grass under the scorching sun was proverbial. Cf Psalm 129:6; Isaiah 40:6-8.
